summary: OpenAI launched Presence, an enterprise product that deploys voice and chat AI agents with policies, guardrails, simulations, and a Codex-powered improvement loop to handle customer and internal support workflows.

mechanisms.reason: The product replaces human agents handling support requests with AI agents that take approved actions and escalate only when needed, with a stated resolution rate.
mechanisms.quote: Within weeks, it met or exceeded benchmarks we use to grade frontline human-support quality and now resolves 75% of inbound issues without human assistance.

practices.reason: The Codex-powered improvement loop that investigates production signals and proposes agent policy updates is a concrete orchestration pattern, but it is tied to OpenAI's own proprietary product and not yet self-serve.
practices.quote: Codex using the Presence plugin investigates those signals and suggests updates. Teams can test each proposed change against the version in production, then approve a controlled rollout.

practices.reason: The described pre-launch testing regime (simulations and graders checking outcome, policy adherence, tool use, and escalation) is a transferable evaluation pattern for agentic systems, though it is described as OpenAI's internal process rather than handed over as an instrument.
practices.quote: Simulations and graders check whether it reached the right outcome, followed policy, used tools correctly, and escalated when appropriate.

practices.reason: Presence requires OpenAI Forward Deployed Engineers or systems integrators to deploy and is not self-serve, which limits direct integration work for most teams.
practices.quote: Presence is not yet available as a self-serve product.
